audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers say Kassadin has to wait out Twisted Advance — 'R lets you blink out the instant it expires', 'you can't sidestep the instant W root itself'. Riftwalk is a blink, and roots do not disable blinks.
audit.why: This is the load-bearing error of the matchup. A rooted unit cannot move or dash but can still cast blinks and teleports; the wiki lists grounding, not rooting, as what disables Riftwalk. So Maokai landing his W does not buy him the free window the page promises — Kassadin leaves immediately, which changes every post-6 exchange and every gank in this lane.
audit.corrected: Written into spikes[1].text, whys[4], phases[4].why, wants.you[0], content.mid, breakdown.mid, tradeGood and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sap Magic's cooldown reduction is absent everywhere. Riot's text: 'Each time Maokai casts a spell OR IS STRUCK BY AN ENEMY'S SPELL, this cooldown is reduced.'
audit.why: It inverts the poke logic. Every speculative Null Sphere Kassadin throws at Maokai accelerates the heal he is trying to out-chip — so aimless poke in this lane is worse than not poking at all. The pages tell him to shield and farm but never explain why his harass does nothing.
audit.corrected: Stated in tradeBad, breakdown.early, dontsFull[1].d, wants.foe[1], whys[2], content.early and the itemization block's anti-heal line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance makes Maokai untargetable for the duration of the dash. Neither layer mentions it.
audit.why: Null Sphere is a targeted ability. A Kassadin who reflexively Qs the incoming W wastes his shield, his mana and his only pre-6 tool on a unit that cannot be targeted, then eats the root with nothing left.
audit.corrected: Added to dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns, content.early and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0] through [6] are the generic Kassadin boilerplate — 'your worst level in the game', 'the survival grind' — and none of them mentions that Maokai has no gap-closer until level 2 or what any of his cooldowns are.
audit.why: Level 1 is genuinely the safest minute of this lane because Twisted Advance does not exist yet; the boilerplate calls it his worst level. Level 2 is the actual danger and the page gives it the mildest description on the chart.
audit.corrected: All seven phase reasons rewritten around Twisted Advance's 14/13/12/11/10s clock and the blink interaction.

audit.whatIsWrong: content win[] and full phases[] hand Maokai first item AND two-plus items, on a lane the same page's own late-game text opens with 'You own this' and which sits at 69.23% for Kassadin. The packet's levelChart says Kassadin owns all three of the last stages.

audit.corrected: Cannot be applied — see notes. Flagged for a hand fix.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block said only 'count its cooldown before stepping up' with no number, for any ability.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1 falling to 10, Bramble Smash 7s to 5, Nature's Grasp 130/110/90s. The 14-second figure is the whole green-light system and it was never printed.
audit.corrected: All three added to breakdown.cooldowns, plus dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, tradeGood, phases[3] and All-In Windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two stale Kassadin numbers repeat here: Void Stone described as '15% magic reduction' in spikes[3] and content.late and whys[6], and phases[2].why's 'E only charges when spells fly'.
audit.why: Void Stone has been 10% since V11.24, and Force Pulse stopped being charge-gated in V12.23 — it is a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown that nearby ability casts shorten by a second each. The kit file still carries the pre-rework tooltip text, which is how the error survives.
audit.corrected: 15% set to 10% in all three places (identical length, applies cleanly); phases[2].why rewritten to the cooldown model.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late tells the player to 'Q-silence the counterplay', and content.spikes[2]/wants.you[1] claim Nether Blade gives a 'quintupled mana refund'.
audit.why: Null Sphere has no silence — Riot's text is damage, a channel interrupt and a magic shield. And no multiplier for Nether Blade's mana restore appears in Riot's description; I could not source the figure.
audit.corrected: Silence replaced with the shield; the multiplier dropped and the mechanic kept.

edits.before: Maokai owns the early window and it is the only real danger here. Once he hits 2 he has W (Twisted Advance), a point-and-click dash-root: over-extend for a cannon and he locks you, Q-knockbacks, and drops an E sapling on top while you have nothing but Null Sphere and no dash to leave. Don't trade autos near his saplings — last-hit at max range and eat the chip. Null Sphere's shield can soak one sapling proc if you're forced to take it, but mana is precious pre-RoA, so spend it on safety, not poke you can't follow up on. Watch for a flash-W all-in.
edits.after: Maokai owns the early window and it is the only real danger here. Once he hits 2 he has W (Twisted Advance), a point-and-click dash-root — and he is untargetable for the whole dash, so a reflex Null Sphere at the incoming W simply fizzles. Over-extend for a cannon and he locks you, Q-knockbacks, and drops a sapling on top. Don't trade near his saplings; last-hit at max range and eat the chip. And don't free-poke him: every spell that strikes Maokai shortens Sap Magic, so your harass pays for his healing.

edits.before: This is the turn. Level 6 Riftwalk answers what he does — you can't sidestep the instant W root itself, but R lets you blink out the moment it expires or leave before he ever dashes in, so his sapling-set ganks stop being free kills. Don't fight him straight yet; he still trades fine into a pre-item Kassadin thanks to Sap Magic sustain. Once Rod of Ages comes online and Nether Blade is refunding the mana his chip drains, you out-sustain the poke and the lane flips to even. Bait his W cooldown — once it's down he's a slow, immobile tree you simply walk away from.
edits.after: This is the turn. Level 6 Riftwalk answers what he does — and not by waiting out the root. Riftwalk is a blink and roots do not disable blinks, so the moment his W lands you simply leave, and his sapling-set ganks stop being kills. Don't fight him straight yet; he still trades fine into a pre-item Kassadin thanks to Sap Magic sustain, and every spell you land on him only shortens it. Once Rod of Ages is online and Nether Blade is refunding the mana his chip drains, the lane flips to even. Bait his 14-second W — down, he is a slow, immobile tree you walk away from.

His only tool against you is a single W root, so respect its cooldown in skirmishes — bait it, then assassinate everything behind him. Unlike Vladimir or Kayle, he doesn't out-scale you, so your dominance only grows.
